answer: Identities cost only a signature here, so this economy prices them in time. Each answer must run a sequential delay, where every step depends on the last, plus a proof verifiers check in milliseconds without redoing the work. Parallel hardware cannot shorten that chain, so a thousand keys need a thousand serial runs inside one short window. A false identity then costs hardware, elapsed time and an unfakeable proof, none recoverable. Trust alone is a karst, solid on the surface and hollow beneath; a fast-checked proof is the summit, reached only by walking. Work proven this way sets in basalt.
